response.consequence: The log sent to Seer places all errors at the start of the timeline, so the summary misattributes when errors occurred relative to user actions.
response.explanation: gen_request_data compares error_events[i]['timestamp'] with event.get('timestamp', 0) for each replay event. Error timestamps come from nodestore event data, where they are epoch seconds (about 1.7e9). Replay recording events (rrweb) use epoch milliseconds (about 1.7e12). The two values are in different units, so every error compares as earlier than every replay event. All errors are emitted before the first replay event's message, and the chronological interleaving the code promises never happens. I did not read the nodestore event schema or the replay event format, so the unit mismatch rests on my knowledge of both formats.

other_findings.consequence: With more than one page of segments, the same error messages are duplicated in each page's Seer request and in each summary.
other_findings.explanation: analyze_recording_segments is used as on_results for a paginated response and runs once per page. Each call passes the full error_events list to gen_request_data. Errors earlier than the page's first event are emitted at the start of every page. Errors later than the page's last event are emitted at the end of every page. In both cases the same errors are repeated across pages.
other_findings.title: All error events are re-emitted on every paginated page

other_findings.consequence: ErrorEvent.id can be wrong when some error nodes are missing. The id is not used in the log message, so the effect is small.
other_findings.explanation: nodestore.get_multi returns a dict keyed by node id. Missing nodes may be omitted from that dict, and the values are not guaranteed to follow the order of error_ids. In either case zip(error_ids, events.values()) pairs the wrong id with the data. I did not check the nodestore backend implementation to see whether it omits missing keys.
other_findings.title: zip of error_ids with get_multi values can misalign ids

response.consequence: When the trace-items/attributes request fails, consumers see a loading state for several seconds, and the endpoint gets about four requests instead of one.
response.explanation: The old hook called useApiQuery with retry: false. The new hook calls the raw useQuery with only enabled, queryKey and queryFn. DEFAULT_QUERY_CLIENT_CONFIG sets only refetchOnReconnect and refetchOnWindowFocus, so react-query's default of 3 retries with exponential backoff now applies. If the attributes endpoint returns an error, useGetTraceItemAttributeKeys throws, the query retries, and isFetching (exposed as isLoading) stays true until the retries finish. During that time attributes is the previous value, and error is not set until the last retry fails.
